newsitem.title: CHINA: China B share indices tumble, following A shares.
newsitem.headline: China B share indices tumble, following A shares.

text.p: China's foreign B share indices plunged on Thursday, following steep falls on the domestic A share market triggered by rumours of more Beijing plans to rein in the markets, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index closed down 2.914 points or 3.70 percent at 75.776 points and the Shenzhen B index dived 8.74 points or 6.04 percent to 135.97.
The Shanghai A index closed down 50.731 points or 4.05 percent at 1,202.283 while Shenzhen's A share index plummeted 22.85 points or 5.30 percent to 408.27 after losing 4.07 percent on Wednesday.
"Institutions are pulling funds out of the market on the expectation of imminent new measures from Beijing to eliminate stock speculation," Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Rumours sweeping the market said the government would announce more steps to stop state firms speculating in stocks and would allow some types of currently non-tradable shares to be listed.
The recent faster pace of new share listings, absorbing large amounts of liquidity from the markets, exacerbated the retreat, brokers said.
"On the A share market, new listings sucked up a lot of capital, which is one of the reasons for the poor performance of existing shares these last two days," a Shanghai broker said.
"The pace of fresh money inflow is not able to keep pace with that of new listings due to the absence of large institutions from the market," the Guotai broker said.

"Investors were seen selling in Pudong shares heavily (in the Shanghai B share market), especially in Lujiazui, which had risen shapply over the past few months," said one local broker. "That pushed down the (Shanghai) B index."
Brokers said Pudong-related shares looked over-priced following recent rises.
The conclusion of the Hong Kong handover, which has long been a major support for sentiment, also capped buying interest, brokers said.
"More investors pulled out and moved to the sidelines after the handover euphoria failed to produce a miracle in yesterday's A share market," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Brokers said a rebound is possible in the near future after sharp falls over the past two sessions, but sentiment remains weak.
Investors are now looking towards positive interim results for an excuse to buy following the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule at midnight on Monday, which sparked a rally earlier this year.
In Shanghai, Pudong developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co ended down $0.074 or 5.48 percent to $1.276 to become one of the day's top B share losers.
In the Shenzhen B share market, floppy disk maker Shenzhen Benelux was the weakest performer with a loss of HK$0.34 to its 10 percent limit-down at HK$3.06.
In its A share market, market barometer Shenzhen Development Bank dropped 1.33 yuan to 34.80 yuan on heavy volume of 14 million shares after hitting a low of 34.55 yuan.
